facts.text: These have all been getting worse.

aliases: how long the symptoms have been going on
facts.text: The symptoms began about two weeks after I started taking Sai-rei-to.
I started a herbal medicine called Sai-rei-to 25 days ago.
I don't take any other medicines.
I used to smoke, but I've stopped.
I've never had any lung disease.
Both of my lower legs are swollen.

findings.result: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage with a neutrophil predominance: total cell count 325,000/mL (62% neutrophils, 26% lymphocytes, 12% macrophages); CD4/CD8 ratio 0.49.

gold.reasoning: 1. Drug-induced lung injury by Sai-rei-to was most likely — “Drug-induced interstitial lung disease (ILD) caused by Sai-rei-to was the most likely diagnosis, because he had no history of interstitial pneumonia or collagen disease, and he had started taking Sai-rei-to a month earlier.” 2. Community-acquired pneumonia was considered but microbiology was unrevealing — “Bacteriological tests did not detect any bacterial or viral pathogens.” 3. Pulmonary vasculitis (Goodpasture syndrome or ANCA-associated vasculitis) was considered because of alveolar hemorrhage — “As his BAL findings suggested alveolar hemorrhage, we considered an alternative diagnosis of Goodpasture syndrome or ANCA related vasculitis.”

leakage.reason: Explicit denial of previous pulmonary disease (s003); 'lung' is the organ word, not the diagnosis.

source_issues: A fourfold rise in the Mycoplasma complement fixation titer suggests recent Mycoplasma infection, while the reasoning calls the microbiology unrevealing.
Oxygen saturation 99% on 12 L/min sits oddly with 'severe hypoxemia' on the blood gas; the two may have been taken at different times or oxygen settings.
s014 says 'all oral therapies including Sai-rei-to were discontinued', which sits oddly with 'took no other medications' (s003).
notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation with progressive dry cough, dyspnea, fever and chills about 25 days after starting Sai-rei-to (s001-s011); bronchoalveolar lavage (s013) came after admission and oxygen therapy and is a finding with time.
The symptom onset is kept as stated (two weeks after starting Sai-rei-to), not converted to days before presentation.
